Consult Summary:
- Postpartum patient with new, acute shortness of breath after cesarean delivery; further assessment recommended for possible postpartum venous thromboembolism; patient agreed to go to hospital for evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath started about 1 hour ago while resting; associated cough began yesterday; patient reports chest soreness on deep breath and tender C-section scar; no chest pain reported.
- Onset/duration/progression: SOB began hours ago and persistent; cough started yesterday; heart racing sensation noted.
- Medical history/medications/allergies: Recent cesarean section 4 weeks ago. Allergic to ibuprofen. Postpartum pain managed with codeine; taking codeine fairly regularly but not in the last week. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Lives with a baby (4 weeks postpartum); partner at work; currently alone at home.
- Other: No other medical problems documented; patient denies current fever or flu-like symptoms.

Examination:
- Not documented. No clinician-obtained vitals provided beyond the patient’s self-reported home heart-rate check.

Impression:
- Working impression: Acute shortness of breath in the postpartum period with concern for possible venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE) given recent cesarean delivery; requires hospital evaluation.

Plan:
- Management/treatment: Recommend hospital assessment. Patient can self-transport with baby; ambulance available if desired. Do not take codeine for the time being.
- Instructions: Bring baby and essentials to the hospital; monitor symptoms. If clot suspected, hospital can initiate treatment (anticoagulation) as appropriate.
- Follow-up: Not specified; hospital evaluation is prioritized.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Comprehensive past medical history and ROS beyond postpartum status; complete medication list with doses/routes/frequencies; documented vitals (BNP, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, etc.); physical examination findings; clear allergy list beyond ibuprofen; explicit follow-up plan or disposition instructions beyond hospital referral.
- Internal conflicts: None detected.
- Transcript quality: Some informal dialogue and minor repetition; no major inaudible sections.
